summary: Cynthia Col specializes in religious studies, sinology, and tibetology. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.
Cynthia M. Beall is a tibetologist who studied at Pennsylvania State University from around 1972 to 1976. In 1976, she joined Case Western Reserve University.

Cynthia Talbot is an indologist and historian who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1979 to 1988. She became a professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin, where she held a post from around 1997.

Historian and indologist Cyril Henry Philips studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS. He succeeded Ralph Lilley Turner as Director of SOAS in 1957 and later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London from 1972 to 1976.

Cyrus Stearns is a tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, also studying under Turrell V. Wylie. He has served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher works in tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein and served as a research fellow there.

Sinologist and philosopher D. C. Lau studied at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Glasgow. He held appointments at SOAS, University College London, and the University of London, before serving as Chair at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
D. C. Sarasvati was an indologist who studied under V. Raghavan. From 1964 to 1965, she served as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras.
D. L. Narasimhachar was a scholar of linguistics and indology who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore. He held a post at the University of Mysore from around 1932 to 1962.

D. Max Moerman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, japanology, and religious studies. He has served at Barnard College and Columbia University, where he is attested as Professor and Chair of the Department of Asian and Middle Eastern Cultures.
Indologist D. N. Shukla earned a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer. He was affiliated with Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University in 1958.

D. Neil Schmid works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Waseda University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a doctoral student of Victor H. Mair.

D. Phillip Stanley is a tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He served as associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute.

Dagfinn Føllesdal studied at the University of Oslo and Harvard University under Willard Van Orman Quine. In philosophy and linguistics, he taught at Harvard, became Professor Emeritus at the University of Oslo, and held an endowed chair at Stanford University.

Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar of tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg from 2007 to 2017 under Dorji Wangchuk. She became a professor at Leipzig University around 2022.

Taichi Tado specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and indology. As of 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Daiei Kaneko was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa at Otani University. He later taught at Toyo University, served at Otani University from around 1916 to 1953, and founded Koho Gakuen.
Daigo Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who was affiliated with Ryukoku University as a research student (研究生) in 2006.

Daijaku Judith Kinst is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She served on the faculty at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and is attested as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 2026.

Daijo Tokiwa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, and founded the Koa Buddhist Culture Research Institute.
